passages.title: A garden above the street
passages.body: [1] When the community center reopened, its roof was still an empty rectangle of dark gravel. [2] Volunteers laid out six shallow beds, and they planted native flowers beside the path. [3] The roof receives little shade, so the volunteers installed a rain barrel beside the stairwell. [4] They also set up two benches that face the street. [5] By midsummer, neighbors were bringing their lunches upstairs. [6] The wind sometimes made conversation difficult, but visitors stayed. [7] The original plans had called for a seventh bed, which the volunteers omitted to give the benches more space. [8] At the end of the season, the center invited visitors to suggest the next change.

passages.title: Cataloging a repaired radio
passages.body: [1] The museum acquired a wooden radio that had belonged to the same family for three generations. [2] Before putting the radio on display, Mara photographed every side of its case. [3] The photos showed a dark patch behind the tuning dial. [4] A family letter explained that a repair shop had replaced the original dial in 1948. [5] Mara compared the letter with the repair shop’s account book. [6] The date in the book matched the date in the letter. [7] Consequently, she revised the display label to describe the substitution. [8] Visitors could now see how the family had kept an old device working long after its original parts failed.

passages.title: A workshop builds a kayak
passages.body: [1] Every Saturday in spring, volunteers at a boat workshop fitted thin strips of cedar over a frame. [2] The strips were numbered, but a few had warped in storage. [3] To keep the seams flush, the crew trimmed the warped strips before gluing them. [4] Jo checked the fit by running a finger along each seam. [5] The crew sanded the hull once the glue had dried. [6] After they finished sanding, they covered the wood with a thin cloth and clear resin. [7] Some volunteers wanted to paint the finished hull bright orange. [8] The team kept the transparent finish so that visitors could see the cedar strips. [9] At the launch, the kayak floated level beside the dock.

passages.title: A bicycle clinic learns to teach
passages.body: [1] The neighborhood bicycle clinic opened with a table of spare parts and one shared repair stand. [2] At first, visitors handed over a bicycle and waited while a volunteer repaired it. [3] The volunteers soon noticed that the same flat tires returned every week. [4] They began asking visitors to remove the wheels and find the leaks themselves. [5] A volunteer explained each step, but the visitor did the work. [6] Repairs took longer under the new approach. [7] Two months later, the volunteers counted fewer return visits for the same problem. [8] The clinic still kept spare parts on hand because learning to mend a tire sometimes required a replacement tube.

passages.title: The field recorder
passages.body: [1] Years ago, recording dawn bird calls meant carrying a heavy recorder to the marsh before sunrise. [2] Now a technician can leave a small device overnight and collect it in the morning. [3] Each device stores a short recording every quarter hour. [4] The recordings capture birds, wind, and the sound of nearby trains. [5] Nia labels those other sounds so that researchers can find the calls more easily. [6] She notes the start time of each train and records how long it remains audible. [7] Her notes show that a particular bend in the tracks produces a long metallic squeal. [8] What originally looked like an obstacle has become a second source of information.

items: In sentence 1, which word could replace “reopened” to emphasize that the center had operated previously?
Resumed operations explicitly means started operating again.
Which revision to the middle of sentence 2 correctly uses a semicolon?
beds; native flowers beside the path
beds; the volunteers planted native flowers
beds; that they planted with native flowers
Both sides of a semicolon must be independent clauses. Only the third choice supplies a complete clause after it.
The writer wants to show two ways the volunteers made the roof usable to visitors. Which detail in sentence 4 best serves that purpose?
The benches were assembled with metal fasteners.
The benches arrived in a borrowed van.
The path lets visitors reach benches that face the street.
The stairwell was painted last spring.
A path and places to sit describe two ways visitors can actually use the space.
Which choice could replace “so” in sentence 3 while preserving the relationship between the clauses?
A sunny roof was the reason for adding a supply of water. As a result signals that direction of cause and effect.
Where should sentence 7 be placed to put the design explanation next to the feature it explains?
Sentence 4 introduces the benches. Putting the design explanation immediately after it clarifies why they have space.
Which word most precisely replaces “bringing” in sentence 5 if the writer means the neighbors physically moved lunches upstairs?
Carrying specifies physical transport to the roof.
Which version of sentence 6 joins the same two clauses with standard punctuation?
The wind sometimes made conversation difficult, visitors stayed.
The wind sometimes made conversation difficult visitors stayed.
The wind sometimes made conversation difficult; however, visitors stayed.
The wind; sometimes made conversation difficult, but visitors stayed.
The semicolon joins two independent clauses, and the comma sets off however.
Which wording most concisely preserves the meaning of “At the end of the season” in sentence 8?
At the close and conclusion of the season
In the middle of the season
At season’s end keeps the timing while removing unnecessary words.
Which edit would turn sentence 4 into a fragment if it stood alone?
Locating two benches by the path, the volunteers faced them toward the street.
The volunteers also set up two benches.
Two benches that face the street.
The relative clause that face the street modifies benches. The final choice lacks a main verb.
Which addition to the last sentence would best connect the invitation to the passage’s theme of ongoing community use?
The new suggestions included a shade sail over the benches at lunchtime.
The invitation was printed on white paper.
The center paid for toner in October.
The gravel had a different color in the original photograph.
A shade sail meets a need of the lunchtime visitors already mentioned, connecting future plans with current use.
In sentence 2, what does “its” refer to?
The case contains the radio. The phrase “of its case” refers to the radio’s case.
In sentence 4, why is “had replaced” the appropriate form?
The replacement was a future plan.
The replacement happened before the letter explained it.
The museum made the replacement while Mara photographed the radio.
The past perfect marks an event that happened earlier than another past event, the letter’s account of it.
Which wording uses a possessive correctly to describe one repair shop’s account book?
Add apostrophe-s to the singular owner shop.
Which revision of sentence 6 preserves that Mara looked at two dates and found them identical?
The dates in the two sources matched.
The dates matched alike in both of the two sources.
The letter was older than the book.
The sources dated back to different years.
The first choice states the shared date directly and keeps both sources in view.
Which connector could replace “Consequently” in sentence 7 if the verified date was the reason for the revision?
Therefore expresses the consequence of verifying the date.
Where would the sentence “The book listed every radio the shop repaired that year” best clarify how the new source was useful?
Sentence 5 first introduces the account book. The addition explains why its entries could confirm the date.
Which phrase could replace “describe the substitution” in sentence 7 without changing its meaning?
explain the removal of the entire radio
explain the replacement of the dial
name the owner of the repair shop
The substitution refers to installing a replacement tuning dial.
Which verb correctly completes “The photographs of the wooden case ___ a dark patch”?
The plural subject photographs takes show.
The writer considers adding “The museum walls were repainted the previous fall” after sentence 7. Should the writer add it?
Yes, it explains why the dates matched.
Yes, it shows how the radio was repaired.
No, it repeats what the label says about the dial.
No, it distracts from the account of documenting the radio.
The paint detail does not clarify the repair, supporting evidence, or exhibit label.
Which standalone sentence correctly joins the two actions with a single shared subject?
Mara checked the records and updated the label.
Mara checked the records, she updated the label.
Mara checked, the records and updated the label.
Checking the records and updating the label.
The subject Mara governs both verbs in the first choice. A comma alone cannot join complete independent clauses.
Which word most precisely replaces “warped” in sentence 2 if the strips had lost their intended shape?
Bent conveys a change in shape that makes the strips difficult to fit.
Which portion correctly punctuates sentence 2 where two independent clauses join?
Place the comma before the coordinating conjunction but to separate the clauses.
Which revision makes clear that Jo ran a finger along each seam?
Running a finger along each seam, the fit was checked.
Running a finger along each seam, Jo checked the fit.
The fit, running a finger along each seam, was checked by Jo.
Each seam ran a finger along Jo to check the fit.
The introductory phrase must modify the person performing the action, Jo.
Which wording could replace “After they finished sanding” in sentence 6 while keeping the timeline?
After sanding preserves which process was completed first.
Which transition at the beginning of sentence 8 best contrasts the group’s decision with the suggestion in sentence 7?
Instead signals the group chose the clear finish in place of painting the hull orange.
The writer wants to add “The builders brought the kayak to the dock for a trial on the first warm day of May.” Where does it best fit?
The sentence sets up the launch described in sentence 9, after the construction and finishing steps.
Which wording uses parallel forms in a list of the crew’s tasks?
trimming strips, sand the hull, and coating the wood
trimmed strips, sanded the hull, and coated the wood
trimming strips, the hull was sanded, and they coated the wood
trimmed strips, sanding the hull, and coat the wood
All three verbs in the second choice are in the same past-tense form.
Which addition to sentence 9 best demonstrates the success of the crew’s fitting work?
A crowd gathered beside the dock.
The crew chose a quiet morning for the launch.
No water seeped through the seams.
Several volunteers had paddleboards at home.
Watertight seams are direct evidence that the strips fit and were attached effectively.
Which verb completes “The resin on the finished cedar strips ___ the grain visible” in standard present tense?
Resin is the singular subject. Strips belongs to a modifying prepositional phrase.
Which alternative to “the kayak floated level” best matches the passage’s factual tone?
the kayak stayed even in the water
the boat had a totally epic first day
the craft was obviously the best ever made
the majestic vessel conquered the river
Only the first choice reports an observable result in the same restrained style.
Which word most precisely replaces “waited” in sentence 2 if the writer means visitors stayed nearby until the repairs ended?
Remained expresses staying in a place for the duration of the repairs.
Which connector best introduces sentence 4 if it presents the volunteers’ response to the issue in sentence 3?
In addition to the spare parts,
The change in teaching responds directly to the recurring repairs.
Which wording most concisely replaces “the visitor did the work” while preserving who performed it?
the person visiting did all of the work that was done
The visitor worked retains the actor and removes the redundant did the work.
Which wording completes a sentence with a correctly punctuated example introduced by a colon?
Visitors learned: to remove wheels and find leaks.
Visitors learned two skills: removing wheels and finding leaks.
Visitors learned two: skills removing wheels and finding leaks.
Visitors learned two skills removing: wheels and finding leaks.
A colon may introduce a list after a complete clause. “Visitors learned two skills” is a full clause.
Which detail would most directly support the result reported in sentence 7?
The volunteers borrowed a pump from a neighbor.
The clinic moved one table closer to an outlet.
The record shows 12 repeat visits before the change and 4 afterward in equal-length periods.
Visitors often arrived in groups of two.
Comparable before-and-after counts directly support a decrease in repeat visits.
Where should “The longer appointments let volunteers watch visitors try the steps on their own” be placed?
The addition explains a benefit of the longer repairs that sentence 6 introduces.
Which list consistently uses infinitives to describe the skills taught?
to remove wheels, to find leaks, and to patch tubes
to remove wheels, finding leaks, and patched tubes
removing wheels, to find leaks, and tubes are patched
remove wheels, leaks to find, and to patch tubes
The full infinitive form to plus a base verb appears in all three positions in the first choice.
Which opening to sentence 7 best highlights the contrast with the drawback in sentence 6?
For the same reason, after two months
Nevertheless contrasts the longer individual repairs with the later decrease in repeat visits.
In sentence 4, who is referred to by “themselves”?
the owners of the spare parts
The visitors are asked to perform the two repair steps themselves.
Which concluding sentence best reflects the clinic’s shift in purpose?
The repair stand was eventually painted green.
The clinic gradually became a place to learn a repair instead of merely waiting for one.
The spare parts had been delivered on the first day.
A single shared repair stand occupies little space.
The passage centers on moving from volunteers fixing bikes to visitors learning the fix.
Which word could replace “collect” in sentence 2 to emphasize physically taking the device back after use?
Retrieve means go and bring something back, which fits the overnight setup.
Which version correctly adds commas to set off a nonessential detail about the already identified bend?
The bend, which lies north of the marsh, produces a squeal.
The bend, which lies north of the marsh produces a squeal.
The bend which lies north of the marsh, produces a squeal.
The bend which lies, north of the marsh produces a squeal.
The nonessential relative clause is bounded by commas on both sides.
Which phrase most concisely replaces “every quarter hour” in sentence 3 without changing the timing?
A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.
Which detail best explains why labeling train sounds is helpful to bird researchers?
A loud train can mask a call recorded in the same interval.
The technician reaches the marsh by walking.
Identifying intervals with masking noise helps researchers find or interpret bird calls.
Which verb phrase best completes “When dawn arrived yesterday, the recorder ___ running for six hours”?
Had been running denotes an activity that began earlier and continued up to a specified past moment.
Which transition before sentence 2 most clearly emphasizes the contrast in equipment over time?
By comparison contrasts the earlier heavy recorder with the current small one.
Which list would describe Nia’s actions with parallel verb forms?
labels winds, timing trains, and to identify calls
to label winds, timed trains, and identifying calls
labels wind, times trains, and identifies calls
labeling wind, trains are timed, and Nia identifies calls
Labels, times, and identifies are parallel present-tense verbs.
Which sentence best introduces the shift from equipment to interpreting recordings immediately after sentence 3?
The clock on the recorder needed charging.
Recording sounds is only the beginning of sorting them.
The technician has owned three umbrellas.
The marsh grew larger in the spring.
The addition connects the device’s sampling to the analysis of different sounds in sentences 4–7.
In sentence 6, “it” most naturally refers to what?
It is the train, more specifically the train’s sound, that remains audible.
Which replacement for sentence 8 best makes the unexpected result concrete?
The equipment was purchased before the marsh study began.
Some of the notes were written on paper.
The researcher liked the marsh best in the morning.
The same recordings now help locate persistent rail noise as well as record birds.
The final option specifies how the recordings supply evidence about train noise in addition to documenting bird calls.
